title: Trust: determinism harness, Hypothesis properties, golden test, warm start

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A config passes the harness: ten fresh processes gave byte-identical manifests. What has that shown?

options.text: That the plan obeys the rules, since a wrong plan would change between runs
options.says: "The harness shows the model repeats itself; it does not show the model is right."

options.text: That the run repeats on this machine and versions, not that its plan is right
options.says: Right: the PASS holds for this machine, this OR-Tools and this Python, and correctness is the properties' job.

options.text: That the run repeats on other machines, since the manifest leaves them out
options.says: The lesson says the PASS holds for this machine and these versions; the manifest records the versions so that a change is known.

options.text: That the plan is the best one, since runs that agree have found the optimum
options.says: The run stops at a 0.1% gap, and the reference plan at zero gap was worth more; agreement is about repeating, not optimality.

origin.section: A Run Is Its Manifest, and the Harness Compares Ten of Them Byte for Byte

questions.stem: The strategy draws a witness plan first and builds each portfolio's limits around it. What does the witness give the property test?

options.text: A start for the solver, which the strategy hands over as a hint
options.says: The witness is never given to the solver; the properties compare the solver's plan with it.

options.text: The expected optimum, which the solver's plan must equal exactly
options.says: The property is "no worse than the witness", not equal to it.

options.text: A portfolio with a plan, so every case tests the solver's answer
options.says: Right: feasible by construction, so none of the 200 cases is wasted on a portfolio with no plan.

options.text: Limits that are all tight, so that every rule binds in every case
options.says: Each limit is drawn either tight or loose, so that every rule gets cases where it binds and cases where it does not.

origin.section: Properties Must Hold on Every Drawn Portfolio

questions.stem: A teammate loosens the run setting's gap from 0.1% to 1% and pushes. Which of the milestone's tests fails?

options.text: The determinism harness, since a looser gap makes the runs disagree
options.says: The gap is a stopping rule that counts the search, so the looser run still repeats; the lesson says the harness passes.

options.text: The property tests, since the plan from a looser gap breaks a rule
options.says: The plan breaks no rule, so every property holds.

options.text: All of them, since each one compares the run with the reviewed plan
options.says: Only the golden test compares with a reviewed answer; the other two passed.

options.text: The golden test, since the plan is valid, repeats, and is worth less
options.says: Right: $584k less, "and nothing else in the suite would have said so".

origin.section: A Golden Record Catches a Regression, Not a Rule Error
